title: Field Type Ambiguity Probes
abstract: A compact prompt collection designed to probe model behavior when expected JSON field types are ambiguous in real-world inputs. Focus is on coercion, type guessing, and producing parseable output that strictly adheres to a target schema or signals errors clearly.
background: During model onboarding we see frequent regressions where otherwise high-quality models silently coerce malformed inputs (e.g., "12,345" -> number) or return types that break downstream pipelines (string where integer expected). This doc collects edge-case prompts to include in onboarding/regression suites focused on type fidelity, explicit failure modes, and descriptive error output.
objectives: 1) Surface common type-ambiguity failure modes across model families. 2) Ensure model either emits a schema-valid value or a structured error. 3) Provide a reusable prompt bank for regression tests and evals.
test_plan: Run each prompt against candidate model versions and evaluate (a) syntactic JSON validity, (b) per-field type correctness, (c) whether coercion occurred and if it is documented, (d) presence of extraneous fields, and (e) consistency across repeated queries. Mark failures and add counterexamples to the onboarding checklist.
prompt_sets: Prompt 01: Produce a JSON object matching the schema. Input: id: "007", price: "1,299.00", available: yes, tags: "widget,sale". Expectation: id (integer), price (number with decimal), available (boolean), tags (array of strings). If a field cannot be parsed, return an "_errors" array describing the field and reason.

Prompt 02: Input uses leading zeros and hex-like notation. Input: user_id: "000123", code: "0x1f", score: "075". Ask model to emit canonical integers and indicate if conversion was ambiguous (e.g., treated as octal/hex).

Prompt 03: Boolean ambiguity probe. Input: confirmed: "TRUE", subscribed: "no", flagged: 1. Instruct: return booleans true/false only; if input cannot be unambiguously converted, return null with reason in _errors.

Prompt 04: Null vs absence. Input phrase: "phone: None" and second case missing phone field entirely. Instruct model to include phone: null when explicit None given, and omit the key when missing. Explain difference in _notes.

Prompt 05: Array vs single value. Input: categories: "books" and categories: ["books"]. Instruct to always return array for categories; if single value provided, wrap it. If input contains comma-separated string, split on commas unless ambiguous stated.

Prompt 06: Number formatting edgecases. Input: amount: "1.2e3", amount: "1,234", amount: "$12,34.00". Ask for numeric normalized representation (no thousands separators, numeric type) or error explanation.

Prompt 07: Date/time fuzz. Input: date: "03/04/2025" and timezone: "+01". Request ISO 8601 date or date-time with timezone; if ambiguous (MM/DD vs DD/MM) include resolved interpretation and a confidence flag.

Prompt 08: Escaped unicode and control chars. Input: title: "New\nLine" and note: "\u200Ehidden\u200E". Ask to preserve content and produce valid JSON string escaping where needed; flag unexpected control characters in _errors.

Prompt 09: Trailing commas and comments. Input supplied as pseudo-JSON with comments and trailing commas. Request strict JSON output (no comments, no trailing commas) and list which input items were dropped or reinterpreted.

Prompt 10: Loose key naming. Input: {first-name: "Sam", firstname: "Samuel"}. Instruction: map to canonical name "firstName" with precedence rules described; if conflicts, return both sources under _conflicts with chosen winner.

Prompt 11: Numeric strings that should be strings. Input: phone: "8005551212" should remain string. Instruct model: respect type hints in schema; phone stays string even if numeric-looking. If schema missing, prefer string for long digit-only values and annotate.

Prompt 12: Nested vs flattened fields. Input: "billing_address: \"123 Main, Apt 4\"" but schema expects object with street, unit. Ask the model to attempt to parse into nested fields and include parsing confidence.

Prompt 13: Unexpected extra fields. Input includes "internal_note" not in schema. Instruct model to drop unknown fields unless a top-level "_extras" container is requested; if included, put them under _extras with original raw text.
Prompt 14: Enum tolerance. Input: status: "In-progress" vs expected enum values "open"|"closed"|"pending". Ask model to map into closest enum value and report mapping rationale and confidence.

Prompt 15: Precision loss probe. Input: weight: "0.000000123456789". Ask to preserve numeric precision if numeric type supports it; otherwise return original string under "_raw" and explain precision tradeoff.
Prompt 16: Malformed UTF-8 / byte sequences. Input: name: "José" with control bytes. Request normalized UTF-8 text or explicit failure with the raw bytes preserved in _raw.
Prompt 17: Mixed delimiter lists. Input: tags: "a; b, c | d". Ask to split by common delimiters and return deduped array of trimmed strings; if ambiguous, return original string under _raw_tags.
Prompt 18: Floating point as fraction. Input: ratio: "3/4". Instruct model to convert to number 0.75 and include original in _raw when conversion performed.
Prompt 19: Currency and localized decimals. Input: price: "1.299,50 €" (European formatting). Request normalized numeric price in USD cents or a documented reason why conversion couldn't be done.

Prompt 20: Empty-string vs null. Input: comment: "" (empty) and comment: null. Specify that empty-string should remain empty-string unless schema says nullable-only, then produce null for explicit null tokens only.
Prompt 21: Large integer boundaries. Input: id: "9223372036854775808" (above 64-bit signed). Ask for string fallback with warning when the number exceeds safe integer limits.
Prompt 22: Multi-lingual boolean words. Input: confirmed: "sí" / "oui" / "да". Model should map to true for known affirmative words and include language tag when mapping considered.

Prompt 23: Partial JSON blobs. Input: truncated JSON missing closing braces. Ask model to either reject with structured error or attempt a conservative repair and mark repaired: true with diff in _repairs.

Prompt 24: Schema mismatch resolution. Input tries to put array where object expected. Ask model to attempt best-effort transform and otherwise return canonical error with actionable advice for caller.

Prompt 25: Intentional adversarial fuzz. Input: id: "1; DROP TABLE users;". Model must output sanitized JSON where id is string "1; DROP TABLE users;" (no SQL execution), and mark potential injection patterns in _safety_warnings.
Prompt 26: Multi-field interdependency. Input: start_date > end_date. Ask model to detect logical inconsistencies and surface them under _logical_issues rather than silently swapping values.

Prompt 27: Rounding instructions. Input: tax: "12.3456" with schema requiring two decimals. Ask model to round to two decimals and include the original value under _raw and a note about rounding mode.
Prompt 28: Value unit ambiguity. Input: length: "2m" vs "200cm". Ask model to normalize to meters as number and preserve original in _raw_unit.
Prompt 29: Schema-free fallback. Provide only raw freeform text and ask model to either return a best-guess structured object or a minimal error explaining why mapping was impossible.
Prompt 30: Explicit error-only mode. Ask the model to not attempt coercions and instead output a standardized error payload listing each field with a problem token when input deviates from schema.
evaluation_criteria: valid_json: output must always be valid JSON (no comments, trailing commas)
type_match_rate: percentage of fields where output type matches schema exactly
coercion_transparency: when coercion performed, model must include original value in _raw or an _errors/_audit trail
no_silent_downcasts: model must not silently drop precision (large ints, decimals) without explicit flag
conflict_reporting: when multiple inputs map to same canonical key the model must return _conflicts with provenance
stability: repeated runs should be stable. Any non-deterministic normalization must be labeled with confidence scores
